messages:
anya: quick heads-up — sdk-android streaming is throwing partial-JSON parse errors for long completions. Alerts show a lot of `Unterminated object` from the JsonReader. Anyone able to triage?

mike: saw the spike in SLO alerts this morning. can you paste the raw chunk pattern and error stack?

anya: sure, here's the minimal log pattern (trimmed):

```
chunk 1: `\{"choices\": { \"index\": 0, \"delta\": { \"content\": \"Hello, this is a long response that will\" } }`
chunk 2: ` continues split across bytes \" and contain emojis \ud83d\ude00\", \"finish_reason\": null } ] }`
error: kotlin.io.IOException: Unterminated object at EOF (JsonReader)
stack: com.redwood.sdk.json.JsonStreamParser.nextObject(JsonStreamParser.kt:112)
```

The server seems to split mid-object (not a problem by itself) but our parser chokes when the client read loop gets bursts and the leftover bytes handling is flawed.

sam: this smells like backpressure / slow consumer. if the read loop keeps allocating and handing partial buffers to the parser without pausing the network source, the parser state and leftover buffer juggling get racy. which socket lib are we using? okHttp?

anya: yes okHttp + okhttp-sse shim; client code is basically reading source.readUtf8() and appending to StringBuilder then feeding our JsonStreamParser on boundary detection.

irene: two quick angles: 1) make the reader truly incremental (feed bytes to parser and keep leftover bytes when parser returns NEED_MORE) instead of string concat; 2) enforce backpressure on the source — pause the read loop when parser backlog > N and resume when drained. In OkHttp you can use BufferedSource.request(n) and only read into buffer when parser can accept it, or use Flow/Channels with limited buffer.

irene: pseudo Kotlin sketch:```kotlin
val buf = Buffer()
val source = body.source()
while (!source.exhausted()) {
  source.read(buf, CHUNK_SIZE)
  while (parser.canParse(buf)) {
    val obj = parser.nextOrNull(buf)
    if (obj == null) break // keep leftover
    handle(obj)
  }
  if (parser.backlog() > HIGH_WATER) {
    // sleep / yield / let coroutine suspend to apply backpressure
    delay(10)
  }
}
```

mike: good call. I'll draft a small change to the Android SDK: replace naive readUtf8 concat with Buffer-backed incremental parser, add a simple high-water counter and a coroutine yield to let the network socket slow down. will open a PR in a bit. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: PR opened — https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-android/pull/482 :eyes:

anya: testing it locally now. quick workaround for services: reduce server chunk size or add an explicit `\n` delimiter between objects so current parser can recover. not ideal but buys time.

sam: also double-check UTF-8 multi-byte boundaries (emoji split) — make sure partial bytes are preserved and not re-decoded mid-codepoint. use byte Buffer, not String, until decoding complete.

mike: noted. I'll include tests that split multibyte characters across reads.

anya: thanks everyone — will report back after PR validation. ping me if you want to pair on integration tests.

mike: pairing this afternoon at 3pm PT to finish tests. :calendar: 3pm?

irene: works for me.

sam: I can join too for flaky-case reproductions.

anya: perfect, see you then.
